properties.name: The first store-touching read after ANY write pays a fixed ~1.1 s, whichever tool it is — 27% of all measured tool time over 47 sessions, paid 417 times, one cause
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-12 on a physical copy of the live store (4,343 nodes / 25,004 edges), reflow2-mcp 0.59.0 release, direct stdio, load 0.1-0.4.

THE BISECT. After one small write (add_decision, ~120 ms):
  describe_schema 7 ms -> get_node 1,175 ms -> get_node 1 ms
  get_node 1,123 ms -> describe_schema 2 ms -> get_node 1 ms
  search_design 1,077 ms -> get_node 47 ms -> get_node 1 ms
  scan_nodes 1,127 ms -> get_node 3 ms
So: describe_schema (touches no store) never pays it; the FIRST read that touches the store pays ~1.1 s; the next store read is back to 1 ms. It is paid ONCE PER WRITE GENERATION, not once per tool.

IT DOES NOT SCALE WITH THE WRITES. First get_node after 1 write: 1,189 ms; after 5: 1,094; after 20: 1,097. A fixed rebuild, not per-write work — whatever is rebuilt is rebuilt whole.

⭐ AND IT IS NOT THE TEXT INDEX. The obvious candidate was a deferred tantivy commit+reload (foundation/text.rs:320 `commit()` -> `reader.reload()`), since search_design pays it. Discriminated: create_edge — a 1 ms RELATION write that indexes no text — is followed by get_node at 1,131 / 1,061 / 1,106 ms, the same tax as after add_decision (1,090 / 1,109). So the rebuild fires on ANY generation bump regardless of what changed, and lives under both the KV read path and the text path. What it rebuilds is NOT located; the spread across runs (~10%) says it is work, not a timer.

WHERE IT IS NOT. Below graph.rs: `derived_at_current_generation` only resets the DerivedMemo (cheap), and detect_gaps recomputed SEPARATELY afterwards at 906 ms, so this is not the gaps/defects memo either.

WHAT IT COSTS, weighted by the 47-session transcript sample (tools/surface_usage.py, 9,335 calls): a store read follows a write 417 times, so this one tax is ~459 s of the ~1,717 s of measured tool time — 27%. It lands on get_node (62 times), export_graph (111), loop_status (120), search_design (53), detect_gaps (47), scan_nodes and detect_defects — and it is the ENTIRE cost of get_node and search_design, whose own cost is 1-2 ms.

⚠️ THE 2026-09-05 BUDGET DID NOT SEE THIS. `con:a-read-after-a-write-costs-at-most-twice-the-same-read-warm` records get_node after a write at 5.3 ms vs 3.7 ms warm, ratio 1.41, and called itself met. Today the same transition measures 1,123 ms vs 1 ms; a second CONSTRAINS edge (cap:store, 1,100, 2026-09-12) now makes the report say `exceeded`, which is the truth. Regression or measurement gap cannot be said from here: tools/time_one_tool.py calls one tool three times with NO write between, so it does not reproduce write-then-read; and the agent-surface profile lists loop_status BEFORE get_node, so loop_status would have absorbed the tax before get_node was timed. No commit since 2026-09-05 touching cache/graph/search is an obvious cause.

BOUNDS: one machine, one store size, one binary; medians of 3-4; the copy carried ~140 throwaway probe nodes from the same session's harnesses.
